newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko wants rouble equal in Minsk, Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko wants rouble equal in Minsk, Moscow.

text.p: Belarus will do everything it can to ensure the Belarussian rouble was worth the same in Minsk and Moscow, President Alexander Lukashenko said in his state of the nation address on Friday.

"There it is worth 30,000 roubles to the dollar, here it stands at 26,000 roubles to the dollar. What's going on here -- a gap!," Lukashenko said. "We are doing everything we can to solve this problem, in talks with Moscow."
The two rates would equalise by mid-year, Lukashenko predicted.

He said he would order all central bank information to remain under wraps to stop banks speculating, accusing them of selling dollars on the Minsk Interbank Currency Exchange when it became clear the bank had run out of reserves.

The president blamed varying rates on mistakes in economic policies of former central bank chief Tamara Vinnikova, who remains in custody after being arrested in January for what state radio called "damage to the state of major proportions."
Lukashenko also forecast a 10 percent increase in foreign investment levels compared to 1996, when Belarus attracted $58.2 million dollars from foreign investors.

Earlier Lukashenko, in a television address late on Thursday, said gross domestic product in the first quarter of this year was nine percent higher than a year earlier, and promised Belarus would proceed slowly in its already slow-moving privatisation programme.
